title: Defects liability period - enforcing builder obligations after possession
p1:
You got the keys to your new home. Does that mean the builder’s responsibility ends there?

Many buyers are surprised to learn that possession is often the beginning of another important phase.
p2: A common misconception is that once a property is handed over, any repair issue becomes the owner’s problem. In reality, the defects liability period gives buyers a window to report certain construction defects and require the builder to address them.
p3:
This period works like a safety net after possession. If problems such as leaks, poor workmanship, faulty fittings, or construction-related defects appear within the agreed period, buyers may have the right to seek corrections from the builder. The key is to document issues early, keep communication records, and understand the terms of the agreement.

A home purchase does not always end at handover. Knowing your post-possession rights can prevent small defects from becoming expensive repairs.
conclusion: Did you know buyers may still have remedies after receiving possession of a property? Have you ever faced a builder refusing to fix a defect?
